hero.title: Annotated Bibliography
hero.summary: A research archive documenting the books, articles, and industry sources that shaped Envue’s brand strategy, visual identity, user experience principles, typography, logo development, sustainability context, and system design.

video.label: Video Synopsis
video.title: Research Overview
video.description: A 60–90 second synopsis explaining the most persuasive research connections behind Envue’s identity system, visual language, and design decisions.

transcript.label: Transcript excerpt
transcript.body: This research phase connects Envue’s major design decisions to twelve selected sources: nine books and three supporting articles. Together, these sources informed the brand strategy, identity standards, emotional tone, typography, visual system, logo refinement, sustainability context, and user experience principles behind the project.

overview.title: Research Framework
overview.body: Research for Envue was organized around a clear relationship between source material, design decisions, and final artifacts. The selected bibliography includes brand strategy texts, identity design references, typography and systems books, UX research, and fashion-related sustainability context. Each annotation explains what the source contributed, how reliable or limited it is, and where its influence appears in the project.

steps.title: Research Source
steps.body: Books, UX articles, and fashion-related research that informed Envue’s development.

steps.title: Design Decision
steps.body: The specific strategic, visual, typographic, experiential, or system-level choice shaped by the research.

steps.title: Envue Artifact
steps.body: The brand strategy, style guide, visual system, logo work, campaign media, or thesis presentation element where the research influence becomes visible.

bibliography.title: Annotated Sources
bibliography.intro: The following twelve sources represent the primary research foundation for Envue. Each annotation includes a summary, evaluation, and reflection that connects the source to a specific design decision and related project artifact.
